audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not be distributable because substantial tax claims rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $814.0 million gross uncertain-tax liability at 2026-06-30, reduced by $408.8 million of estimated offsetting benefits to $405.2 million net; $380.1 million of prior IRS payments is recorded outside cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded settlement attributable to pre-anchor periods reduces the cash and short-term-investment bridge rather than future OE; deducting amounts already funded or captured in OE would double count.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the gross liability for uncertain tax positions, including interest, was $920.8 million and relates primarily to transfer pricing matters.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge adds $4,252.7 million of cash and short-term investments without an explicit tax-claim reserve. The filed liability and new IRS adjustments demonstrate a substantial claim, but the record does not reconcile accruals, offsetting benefits, prior advance payments, and the ultimate cash exposure. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the gross liability alone.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2026-06-30 uncertain-tax liability to the $380.1 million of IRS advance payments, the $412.1 million tax receivable, correlative benefits, penalties and amounts already reflected in OE; rerun the bridge using only the remaining unfunded exposure.

audit_findings.title: The forecast may perpetuate tax benefits that expire in 2032
audit_findings.magnitude: $93.9 million 2025 cash-tax reduction, equal to $0.16 per diluted share and 10.5% of the $893.5 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 tax benefit is embedded in after-tax anchor OE; growing that anchor without a 2032 tax step-up overstates later explicit-period OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has received tax incentives in certain non-United States tax jurisdictions, the primary benefit for which will expire in 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: The expiration is filed, occurs within the ten-year forecast, and the disclosed 2025 benefit is large relative to anchor OE. The valuation method shows no expiration adjustment, so this is reasonably capable of changing the operating valuation, especially because terminal value represents 47.7%–51.5% of operating PV.
audit_findings.action: Determine the incentive-specific 2025 cash-tax benefit expected to disappear, model the expiration year and any replacement incentives or Pillar Two interaction, and rerun all scenarios with the post-2032 cash-tax rate.

audit_findings.title: Temporary transition-services income may be embedded in the permanent OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $63.7 million gross 2025 TSA income, equal to 7.1% of the $893.5 million OE anchor; associated costs and net after-tax contribution are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Finite TSA income recorded in operating income enters 2025 OE and is then grown and carried into terminal value unless removed or faded.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded income from the TSA of $ 63.7 million and $ 30.3 million during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, which was recorded in Other Operating Income on the Company's consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed $63.7 million income is demonstrably temporary, while the valuation reports no perimeter adjustment. Its gross amount is meaningful relative to anchor OE, but the durable overstatement must be measured using the TSA's directly associated costs and taxes. The 2026 filing confirms continuation at a lower $24.7 million for the first half, consistent with a finite runoff.
audit_findings.action: Trace TSA revenue, unfavorable-contract-liability recognition, and directly associated personnel and service costs into 2025 OE; calculate the after-tax net contribution and rerun the scenarios with that contribution fading by the contractual end date.

audit_findings.title: Success-dependent acquisition and development payments are absent from the growth cases
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $1.1 billion of filed contingent payments; the 2026-06-30 filing separately reports up to $332.5 million under business-acquisition agreements; probability-weighted value is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Milestones, royalties and contingent acquisition payments reduce future owner cash flows in the scenarios where the associated products obtain approval or generate sales.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that these contingent payments could be up to $1.1 billion if all milestones or other contingent obligations are met.
audit_findings.explanation: These are conditional future payments rather than demonstrated present liabilities at their maximum amounts. They should be monitored because a successful bull case can trigger both the forecast revenue and its associated cash costs; using the filed maximum as an immediate bridge deduction would overstate the obligation.
audit_findings.action: Map each obligation to the product, approval, sales threshold and forecast year that triggers it; include probability-weighted payments or sales royalties in the same scenario that recognizes the corresponding product benefit.

audit_findings.title: The IP and litigation caption mixes recurring royalties with discrete charges
audit_findings.magnitude: $325.4 million 2025 caption; $300.0 million 2023 upfront payment, $124.0 million prepaid-royalty asset initially recognized, and $8.3 million 2025 prepaid-royalty amortization; annual cash royalties are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back recurring royalties overstates OE, while permanently retaining one-time settlements, impairments or litigation charges understates normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In consideration for the global CNS and related mutual access to certain intellectual property rights, Edwards paid to Medtronic a one-time, lump sum payment of $ 300.0 million and is making annual royalty payments that are tied to net sales of certain Edwards products.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the caption combines economically different items, but the supplied valuation does not disclose which components were retained or normalized in the $893.5 million anchor. Consequently, neither the direction nor the net valuation effect can be established, although the caption is large relative to OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct the 2025 OE adjustment ledger for prepaid-royalty amortization, annual sales-based cash royalties, settlements, contingencies and external legal costs; retain recurring product royalties and normalize only demonstrably discrete charges before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The ten-year OE history may mix current operations with divested businesses
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; reported trend OE of $1,303 million is $409.5 million above the $893.5 million latest-year anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Perimeter inconsistency can distort historical OE growth, volatility and RONTA; under the MIN(trend, latest) rule it would alter the numerical anchor only if a rebuilt trend falls below $893.5 million.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 3, 2024, we sold our Critical Care product group to Becton, Dickinson and Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The divestitures and discontinued-operations recasts are demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether each 2016–2022 OE observation was rebuilt on the continuing-operations perimeter. The current valuation is partly insulated because it anchors to latest OE, which is already below the reported trend, yet a sufficiently lower corrected trend or revised durability judgment could still affect value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every historical OE year to continuing operations, removing Critical Care and the non-core product group cash flows; recompute trend OE, volatility and RONTA, then rerun only if the corrected trend falls below $893.5 million or changes the supported growth cases.
